prompt:
Add a `tasklist` extension: a list item whose text starts with `[ ]`, `[x]` or `[X]` followed by a space becomes a task.
- The marker is replaced by `<input type="checkbox">`, `checked` for `x`/`X`, and `disabled` unless the `clickable` option is true (default false).
- The `<li>` gets the class from the `item_class` option (default `task`).
- It works in ordered and unordered lists, nested lists and loose lists, and keeps inline markup after the marker.
Register it so `markdown.Markdown(extensions=['tasklist'])` works once installed.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer:
I added the `tasklist` extension and registered it, so `markdown.Markdown(extensions=['tasklist'])` works. Its 14 new tests and the full suite pass (1143 tests run, 112 skipped).

- A list item that starts with `[ ]`, `[x]` or `[X]` and a space gets an `<input type="checkbox">`, with `checked` for `x`/`X`.
- The checkbox is `disabled` unless `clickable=True`, and the `<li>` gets the `item_class` class (default `task`); a blank `item_class` adds no class.
- It works in ordered, unordered, nested and loose lists, and keeps inline markup after the marker. In loose lists the checkbox goes inside the item's paragraph.
- The marker is handled before inline parsing, so `[x]` is never read as a reference link, and an escaped `\[x]` is left as text.
- The extension is registered in both `pyproject.toml` and `Markdown-3.11.2.dist-info/entry_points.txt`.

I also added a docs page and a reference page, listed them in `mkdocs.yml` and the extensions index, and put a changelog entry under a new `[unreleased]` heading.
